newsitem.title: UK: C&W retreats as HK Telecom disappoints.
newsitem.headline: C&W retreats as HK Telecom disappoints.

text.p: Cable & Wireless Plc shares dipped on Tuesday as results from majority-owned Hong Kong Telecom fell short of some expectations and the stock came in for profit-taking after last month's sharp rise, analysts said.
The stock was down 8-1/2p at 475 by 1042 GMT in active trading of 1.7 million shares, after yesterday touching its highest level since early May.

John Tysoe, analyst at SocGen, said the HK Telecom results were below some forecasts and that fears of growing competition in the territory had been stoked by a cut-price international service launched by SmarTone Mobile Communications.
"Everyone has suddenly realised that Hong Kong is still there and there are potentially some problems," Tysoe said.
HK Telecom earlier posted a rise in first-half earnings per share to 47.3 HK cents from 43.2 a year earlier.
Recently-floated SmarTone said a new service offered customers savings of up to 57 percent on international calls compared with its previous rates.
James Golob, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said Cable & Wireless was probably due a retreat after its sharp increase last month following the announcement of the cable merger with.
The merger will create C&W Communications, the biggest cable television operator in the UK. "It was terribly overbought on the back of the C&W Communications deal," Golob said.

Analysts said C&W was likely to continue in focus as British Telecom's $20 billion acquisition of the outstanding 80 percent of MCI Communciations prompts talk of further consolidation in the telecoms industry.
"The BT deal raises the stakes for everyone," said Tysoe. "There are going to be more deals around, this is only the beginning."

Yet Oliver Ehrenberg, analyst at Robert Fleming, said he retained a "sell" recommendation on C&W shares because of the threat of increased competition on international call rates and worries over C&W's position in Hong Kong.
"There are huge uncertainties about what will happen to the license in Hong Kong and in addition there are pressures on margins in international telephony," Ehrenberg said.
The Fleming analyst said he did not think the C&W Communications cable deal was necessarily positive. "It doesn't really convince us, we don't see any reason to change our sell stance," he said.
